revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Making Moves
revealWordProblem.text: A group of friends are planning to make a movie. They research the running times of movies made. The data they collected are shown in the histogram. They have asked for your advice on how long their movie should run. What do you recommend? Explain your recommendation based on the data presented in the histogram.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A histogram titled Movie Running Times, with running time in minutes on the horizontal axis and frequency on the vertical axis.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Add up the histogram's frequencies: 7 + 30 + 39 + 22 + 12 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 114 movies total. The tallest bar is the 101–115 minute interval with 39 movies, the mode of the data. Combined with the neighboring 86–100 minute interval (30 movies), that's 30 + 39 = 69 of the 114 movies, or 69 ÷ 114 ≈ 0.605 = 60.5%, running between 86 and 115 minutes. Very few movies run longer than 145 minutes (2 + 1 + 1 = 4 movies, about 3.5%). Based on this data, I'd recommend the friends aim for a running time in the 101–115 minute range, since that's the most common length and keeps their movie in line with most movies made.

questions.stem: A histogram shows these frequencies: 0–4: 3 players, 5–9: 8 players, 10–14: 12 players, 15–19: 5 players. How many players are represented in total?
choiceFeedback: Add all frequencies: 3+8+12+5.
Did you count frequencies or find the highest value?
That total leaves out part of the data. Every bar contributes, so add all four frequencies together — including the shortest bar.
hints: The question asks for the TOTAL across all four intervals — not the tallest bar and not the biggest interval.
Each frequency counts the players in one interval, and no player is counted twice — so combine all four frequencies into one total.
Set up the addition: 3 + 8 + 12 + 5. The sum of all the bar heights is the total number of players.
questions.stemEs: Un histograma muestra estas frecuencias: 0–4: 3 jugadores, 5–9: 8 jugadores, 10–14: 12 jugadores, 15–19: 5 jugadores. ¿Cuántos jugadores se representan en total?
hintsEs: La pregunta pide el TOTAL de los cuatro intervalos, no la barra más alta ni el intervalo más grande.
Cada frecuencia cuenta los jugadores de un intervalo, y ningún jugador se cuenta dos veces, así que combina las cuatro frecuencias en un solo total.
Plantea la suma: 3 + 8 + 12 + 5. La suma de todas las alturas de las barras es el total de jugadores.

questions.stem: In a histogram, what does the height of each bar represent?
choices: The frequency (count) of data in that interval
The average of the data in that interval
questions.explanation: Each bar's height shows the frequency — how many data values fall within that interval.
choiceFeedback: A bar height is not something you calculate from the values — it is something you tally. Think about what you would count to make the bar taller.
Height shows how many—does it show the typical value?
Range is the interval spread, not the height.
hints: Think about what you'd count to draw one bar: you'd tally how many data values land inside that interval.
Height is a COUNT, not a calculation — no averaging, no middle values. Ask which choice simply says 'how many.'
First step: imagine the interval 10–14 holding the values 11, 12, 12, 14. Its bar would rise to 4 — because 4 values fall inside.
questions.stemEs: En un histograma, ¿qué representa la altura de cada barra?
questions.explanationEs: La altura de cada barra muestra la frecuencia: cuántos valores de datos caen dentro de ese intervalo.
choicesEs: La frecuencia (el conteo) de datos en ese intervalo
El promedio de los datos de ese intervalo
hintsEs: Piensa qué contarías para dibujar una barra: contarías cuántos datos caen dentro de ese intervalo.
La altura es un CONTEO, no un cálculo: sin promedios ni valores del medio. Pregunta qué opción simplemente dice 'cuántos'.
Primer paso: imagina el intervalo 10–14 con los valores 11, 12, 12, 14. Su barra llegaría a 4, porque 4 valores caen adentro.

questions.stem: How is a histogram different from a regular bar graph?
choices: Histogram bars touch (no gaps) because the intervals are continuous ranges
Histograms use colors and bar graphs don't
Bar graphs show numbers and histograms show words
questions.explanation: In a histogram, bars touch because each interval connects to the next (0–9, 10–19, etc.) — the data is continuous.
choiceFeedback: There is a real structural difference between the two graphs. Look at the spacing between the bars and at what the horizontal axis is measuring.
Histograms always show intervals—this is the key difference.
Colors don't define a histogram—structure does.
hints: Picture both graphs side by side: one has spaces between its bars, one doesn't. Ask why that would be.
Think about the x-axis: categories like 'red, blue, green' can be separated, but number intervals like 0–9 and 10–19 connect end to end.
First step: write two neighboring intervals, 0–9 and 10–19. Notice that 10 starts right where 9 ends — that's why the bars behave differently.
questions.stemEs: ¿En qué se diferencia un histograma de una gráfica de barras común?
questions.explanationEs: En un histograma las barras se tocan porque cada intervalo se conecta con el siguiente (0–9, 10–19, etc.): los datos son continuos.
choicesEs: Las barras del histograma se tocan (sin espacios) porque los intervalos son rangos continuos
Los histogramas usan colores y las gráficas de barras no
Las gráficas de barras muestran números y los histogramas muestran palabras
hintsEs: Imagina las dos gráficas lado a lado: una tiene espacios entre las barras y la otra no. Pregunta por qué sería así.
Piensa en el eje x: categorías como 'rojo, azul, verde' se pueden separar, pero intervalos numéricos como 0–9 y 10–19 se conectan de punta a punta.
Primer paso: escribe dos intervalos vecinos, 0–9 y 10–19. Nota que el 10 empieza justo donde termina el 9: por eso las barras se comportan distinto.

reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Display Data: Histograms is counting a boundary value in two intervals at once — for example, putting the value 10 in both the '0–9' bin and the '10–19' bin. Each data value belongs to exactly ONE interval. Before you submit, add up all your frequencies and check that the total matches the number of data values you started with.

level1.stem: A histogram has intervals: 0–4, 5–9, 10–14, 15–19. What is the width of each interval?
level1.explanation: Each interval covers 5 values (0,1,2,3,4 then 5,6,7,8,9 etc.), so the width is 5.
choiceFeedback: The width is the span of each interval: 4−0=4 or 5−0=5.
That span covers two intervals joined together. Count the values inside a single interval, from its first number through its last.
Start is 0, end is 4—that's width 4, not 10.
hints: Width means how many whole-number values fit inside one interval — count them, don't just subtract the endpoints.
List the values in the first interval, 0–4: count every whole number from 0 up to and including 4.
Count aloud: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 — how many numbers did you say? Check that the interval 5–9 holds the same amount.
level1.stemEs: Un histograma tiene los intervalos: 0–4, 5–9, 10–14, 15–19. ¿Cuál es el ancho de cada intervalo?
level1.explanationEs: Cada intervalo cubre 5 valores (0, 1, 2, 3, 4 y luego 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, etc.), así que el ancho es 5.
hintsEs: El ancho significa cuántos valores enteros caben dentro de un intervalo — cuéntalos, no solo restes los extremos.
Enumera los valores del primer intervalo, 0–4: cuenta cada número entero desde 0 hasta 4 inclusive.
Cuenta en voz alta: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 — ¿cuántos números dijiste? Revisa que el intervalo 5–9 tenga la misma cantidad.

level1.stem: A histogram bar for the interval 20–29 reaches a height of 7. What does the 7 tell you?
level1.explanation: A bar's height is the frequency — here, 7 values land in the 20–29 interval.
choiceFeedback: The height is not one of the data values itself. It records how many pieces of data landed inside that interval.
Largest value is somewhere in 20–29, not necessarily 7.
Seven intervals would be many—count the intervals shown.
hints: Two numbers appear here: the interval (20–29) and the height (7). Keep straight which one is a range and which is a count.
A bar's height always answers 'how many data values landed here?' Ask yourself what the 7 is counting.
First step: say it as a sentence — 'the bar for 20–29 rises to 7.' Now finish the sentence: '7 what?' Pick the choice that completes it.
level1.stemEs: En un histograma, la barra del intervalo 20–29 llega a una altura de 7. ¿Qué te dice el 7?
level1.explanationEs: La altura de una barra es la frecuencia: aquí, 7 valores caen en el intervalo 20–29.
choicesEs: 7 valores de datos caen entre 20 y 29
hintsEs: Aquí aparecen dos números: el intervalo (20–29) y la altura (7). Ten claro cuál es un rango y cuál es un conteo.
La altura de una barra siempre responde '¿cuántos datos cayeron aquí?' Pregúntate qué está contando el 7.
Primer paso: dilo como oración: 'la barra de 20–29 llega a 7'. Ahora completa la oración: '¿7 qué?' Elige la opción que la complete.

level2.stem: A histogram of test scores shows: 50–59: 2, 60–69: 5, 70–79: 10, 80–89: 8, 90–99: 3. Which interval has the most students?
level2.explanation: The 70–79 interval has the highest frequency of 10 students.
choiceFeedback: Compare: 2, 5, 10, 8, 3—the largest is 10.
5 is less than 10—which bar is tallest?
That interval holds the highest scores, but the question asks where the most students are. Compare the frequencies, not the score ranges.
hints: 'Most students' means the highest frequency — compare the counts 2, 5, 10, 8, 3, not the score ranges themselves.
Careful: the highest scores (90–99) don't mean the most students. Find the largest of the five frequencies first, then read off its interval.
First step: circle the largest number among 2, 5, 10, 8, 3. Then match that count back to its interval — and check the choice pairs both parts.
level2.stemEs: Un histograma de calificaciones muestra: 50–59: 2, 60–69: 5, 70–79: 10, 80–89: 8, 90–99: 3. ¿Qué intervalo tiene la mayor cantidad de estudiantes?
level2.explanationEs: El intervalo 70–79 tiene la frecuencia más alta, con 10 estudiantes.
hintsEs: 'La mayoría de los estudiantes' significa la frecuencia más alta — compara los conteos 2, 5, 10, 8, 3, no los rangos de puntajes.
Cuidado: los puntajes más altos (90–99) no significan la mayor cantidad de estudiantes. Halla primero la mayor de las cinco frecuencias y luego lee su intervalo.
Primer paso: encierra el número más grande entre 2, 5, 10, 8, 3. Luego relaciona ese conteo con su intervalo — y revisa que la opción incluya ambas partes.

level2.stem: A histogram of goals-per-game shows: 0–1: 9 players, 2–3: 6, 4–5: 3, 6–7: 1. What shape is this distribution?
choices: Skewed right (most players low, tail toward high values)
Skewed left (most players high, tail toward low values)
level2.explanation: The tallest bars are at the low end (0–1) and the bars shrink as goals increase — the tail points right, so it is skewed right.
choiceFeedback: A symmetric shape would have the bars mirroring each other around the center. Compare the 9 at the low end with the 1 at the high end.
Are the bars roughly equal height? This isn't symmetric.
Most are low (left), tail goes high (right)—that's right skew.
hints: Sketch the bars: heights 9, 6, 3, 1 from left to right. Notice which side is tall and which way the heights trail off.
Skew is named for the TAIL — the long, low side — not for the peak. Find the direction the bars shrink toward, then name that direction.
First step: the tallest bar (9 players) is at 0–1 goals on the left, and heights fall to 1 by 6–7. Trace the tail with your finger, then name it.
level2.stemEs: Un histograma de goles por partido muestra: 0–1: 9 jugadores, 2–3: 6, 4–5: 3, 6–7: 1. ¿Qué forma tiene esta distribución?
level2.explanationEs: Las barras más altas están en el extremo bajo (0–1) y se van encogiendo a medida que aumentan los goles: la cola apunta a la derecha, así que está sesgada a la derecha.
choicesEs: Sesgada a la derecha (la mayoría de los jugadores abajo, con cola hacia los valores altos)
Sesgada a la izquierda (la mayoría de los jugadores arriba, con cola hacia los valores bajos)
hintsEs: Dibuja las barras: alturas 9, 6, 3, 1 de izquierda a derecha. Fíjate qué lado es alto y hacia dónde bajan las alturas.
La asimetría se nombra por la COLA —el lado largo y bajo—, no por el pico. Halla la dirección hacia donde se encogen las barras y nómbrala.
Primer paso: la barra más alta (9 jugadores) está en 0–1 goles a la izquierda, y las alturas bajan a 1 en 6–7. Traza la cola con el dedo y nómbrala.

level2.stem: Data: 4, 8, 9, 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 22, 24, 27, 31, 33. How many values fall in the 10–19 interval?
level2.explanation: The values 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, and 19 all fall between 10 and 19, so the frequency for that bin is 6.
choiceFeedback: That count sweeps in values from outside the interval. Only numbers from 10 through 19 belong in this bin.
Did you count correctly which values fall in 10–19?
Not all values fit in that interval—count carefully.
level2.stemEs: Datos: 4, 8, 9, 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 22, 24, 27, 31, 33. ¿Cuántos valores caen en el intervalo 10–19?
level2.explanationEs: Los valores 12, 14, 15, 17, 18 y 19 caen entre 10 y 19, así que la frecuencia de ese intervalo es 6.
hints: A frequency is just a count of how many values land inside one interval, endpoints included.
Go through the list in order and mark only the numbers that are at least 10 and no more than 19.
The first value in that range is 12, and 9 is too small to count. Keep working down the list and tally the ones that qualify.
hintsEs: Una frecuencia es simplemente el conteo de cuántos valores caen dentro de un intervalo, incluyendo los extremos.
Recorre la lista en orden y marca solo los números que sean al menos 10 y no más de 19.
El primer valor en ese rango es 12, y el 9 es demasiado pequeño para contar. Sigue bajando por la lista y cuenta los que califican.

level2.stem: Frequencies: 0–9: 3, 10–19: 9, 20–29: 5, 30–39: 2. Which interval has the tallest bar?
level2.explanation: The 10–19 interval has the greatest frequency (9 players), so its bar is the tallest.
choiceFeedback: The tallest bar shows the highest frequency—which interval is it?
That interval sits in the middle of the range, but height depends on the count. Compare the frequencies 3, 9, 5, and 2 directly.
Compare 3, 9, 5, 2—which number is biggest?
level2.stemEs: Frecuencias: 0–9: 3, 10–19: 9, 20–29: 5, 30–39: 2. ¿Qué intervalo tiene la barra más alta?
level2.explanationEs: El intervalo 10–19 tiene la mayor frecuencia (9 jugadores), así que su barra es la más alta.
hints: Bar height comes from the frequency, not from how large the numbers in the interval are.
List the four frequencies on their own and compare them as plain numbers.
The counts are 3, 9, 5, and 2. Decide which of those is greatest and read off the interval it belongs to.
hintsEs: La altura de una barra viene de la frecuencia, no de qué tan grandes son los números del intervalo.
Escribe las cuatro frecuencias por separado y compáralas como números simples.
Los conteos son 3, 9, 5 y 2. Decide cuál es el mayor y lee el intervalo al que pertenece.

level3.stem: A histogram uses intervals 0–9, 10–19, 20–29, and 30–39. A data value of 19 belongs in which interval?
choiceFeedback: 19 is larger than 9, so it cannot sit in that bar. Read the upper bound of each interval.
That interval starts at 20, and 19 is below it. The 10-19 interval includes its endpoint.
Histogram intervals are built so they never overlap, so every value lands in exactly one bar.
level3.explanation: 19 falls between 10 and 19 inclusive, so it belongs in the 10–19 bar. Intervals must not overlap, so every value lands in exactly one.

level3.prompt: A teacher collected test scores and made two different histograms — one with intervals of 5 (50–54, 55–59, etc.) and one with intervals of 20 (50–69, 70–89, 90–109). Both use the same data. How might the two histograms look different? Which interval size gives you more detail about the distribution? When might the larger interval be better?
level3.sentenceFrame: The histogram with intervals of 5 would have ___ bars and show ___. The histogram with intervals of 20 would have ___ bars and show ___. Smaller intervals are better when ___, and larger intervals are better when ___.
level3.hint: Count how many values fall into each interval for both histograms—look at bar heights.
hints: Same data, two bucket sizes. Think: chopping scores into many small buckets vs a few big buckets — what changes about the picture?
Compare three things: how many bars each histogram has, how tall its bars get, and how clearly you can see the shape, peaks, or gaps.
Start with a count: intervals of 5 covering 50–109 make 12 bars; intervals of 20 make just 3. Write what 12 skinny bars reveal that 3 wide ones hide.
level3.explanation: Intervals of 5 across 50–109 make 12 narrow bars with small frequencies, so peaks, gaps, and the exact shape show up clearly. Intervals of 20 make only 3 tall bars that smooth those details away, which is useful when the data set is large or you only want the big-picture comparison of low, middle, and high scores.
level3.explanationEs: Intervalos de 5 a lo largo de 50–109 forman 12 barras angostas con frecuencias pequeñas, así que los picos, los huecos y la forma exacta se ven con claridad. Intervalos de 20 forman solo 3 barras altas que borran esos detalles, lo cual sirve cuando el conjunto de datos es grande o solo quieres la comparación general entre calificaciones bajas, medias y altas.
level3.promptEs: Un maestro recopiló puntajes de exámenes e hizo dos histogramas distintos: uno con intervalos de 5 (50–54, 55–59, etc.) y otro con intervalos de 20 (50–69, 70–89, 90–109). Los dos usan los mismos datos. ¿En qué podrían verse diferentes los dos histogramas? ¿Cuál tamaño de intervalo te da más detalle sobre la distribución? ¿Cuándo podría convenir más el intervalo grande?
hintsEs: Los mismos datos con dos tamaños de intervalo. Piensa: partir los puntajes en muchos grupos pequeños frente a pocos grupos grandes, ¿qué cambia en la imagen?
Compara tres cosas: cuántas barras tiene cada histograma, qué tan altas llegan y qué tan claro se ve la forma, los picos o los huecos.
Empieza con un conteo: intervalos de 5 que cubren 50–109 dan 12 barras; intervalos de 20 dan solo 3. Escribe qué revelan 12 barras delgadas que 3 anchas ocultan.

level3.stem: A histogram of points-per-game has its tallest bars on the LEFT (low scores) and a long tail stretching RIGHT toward a few high scorers. How is this distribution described?
level3.explanation: The tail points right (toward the high values), so it is skewed right — most players are clustered at the low end.
choiceFeedback: It is tempting to name a skew after where the tall bars sit. A skew is named for the direction the long tail stretches instead.
Left skew has the tail on the left, not right.
Symmetric means roughly equal—this has a clear tail.
hints: Underline the two location words in the stem: tallest bars on the LEFT, long tail stretching RIGHT. Skew is named after one of those.
Rule: a distribution is skewed in the direction its TAIL stretches, not where its peak sits. Decide which way the tail points here.
First step: the stem says the tail stretches toward the few high scorers. Apply the tail rule to name the skew — don't follow the peak.
level3.stemEs: Un histograma de puntos por partido tiene sus barras más altas a la IZQUIERDA (puntajes bajos) y una cola larga que se extiende hacia la DERECHA, hacia unos pocos anotadores altos. ¿Cómo se describe esta distribución?
level3.explanationEs: La cola apunta a la derecha (hacia los valores altos), así que está sesgada a la derecha: la mayoría de los jugadores se agrupa en el extremo bajo.
hintsEs: Subraya las dos palabras de ubicación del enunciado: barras más altas a la IZQUIERDA, cola larga que se extiende a la DERECHA. La asimetría se nombra por una de esas.
Regla: una distribución es asimétrica en la dirección hacia donde se extiende su COLA, no donde está su pico. Decide hacia dónde apunta la cola aquí.
Primer paso: el enunciado dice que la cola se extiende hacia los pocos puntajes altos. Aplica la regla de la cola para nombrar la asimetría; no sigas el pico.

level3.stem: Two histograms show the SAME 40 test scores — one uses intervals of 5, the other intervals of 20. Which statement is true?
choices: The interval-of-5 histogram has more bars and shows more detail about the shape
The interval-of-5 histogram leaves some scores out
The interval-of-20 histogram has more bars
Both histograms must look exactly the same
level3.explanation: Smaller intervals create more bars and reveal finer detail; larger intervals smooth the shape into fewer bars. Both still include all 40 scores.
choiceFeedback: Changing the interval width regroups the data but never throws any of it away — all 40 scores still land in some bar.
Wider intervals gather more values into each bar, so they produce fewer bars. Think about how many 20-wide bins it takes to cover the same range.
Smaller intervals show more detail—more bars, finer shape.
hints: Both histograms use all 40 scores — the only difference is bucket width: 5 points vs 20 points per interval.
Reason it out: covering the same score range with narrower buckets requires MORE buckets. Then ask what having more bars does for detail.
First step: take the range 60–79. With width 20 it's ONE bar; with width 5 it becomes four bars (60–64, 65–69, 70–74, 75–79). Compare the detail.
level3.stemEs: Dos histogramas muestran los MISMOS 40 puntajes: uno usa intervalos de 5 y el otro intervalos de 20. ¿Qué afirmación es verdadera?
level3.explanationEs: Los intervalos más pequeños crean más barras y revelan detalles más finos; los intervalos más grandes suavizan la forma en menos barras. Ambos histogramas siguen incluyendo los 40 puntajes.
choicesEs: El histograma con intervalos de 5 tiene más barras y muestra más detalle de la forma
El histograma con intervalos de 5 deja fuera algunos puntajes
El histograma con intervalos de 20 tiene más barras
Los dos histogramas deben verse exactamente iguales
hintsEs: Ambos histogramas usan los 40 puntajes: la única diferencia es el ancho del intervalo, 5 puntos frente a 20 puntos.
Razónalo: cubrir el mismo rango de puntajes con intervalos más angostos requiere MÁS intervalos. Luego pregunta qué logra tener más barras para el detalle.
Primer paso: toma el rango 60–79. Con ancho 20 es UNA barra; con ancho 5 se vuelve cuatro barras (60–64, 65–69, 70–74, 75–79). Compara el detalle.

level3.stem: Data: 4, 8, 9, 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 22, 24, 27, 31, 33. How many values fall in the 10–19 interval?
level3.explanation: The values 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, and 19 all fall between 10 and 19, so the frequency for that bin is 6.
choiceFeedback: That count sweeps in values from outside the interval. Only numbers from 10 through 19 belong in this bin.
Did you count correctly which values fall in 10–19?
Not all values fit in that interval—count carefully.
level3.stemEs: Datos: 4, 8, 9, 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 22, 24, 27, 31, 33. ¿Cuántos valores caen en el intervalo 10–19?
level3.explanationEs: Los valores 12, 14, 15, 17, 18 y 19 caen entre 10 y 19, así que la frecuencia de ese intervalo es 6.
hints: A frequency is just a count of how many values land inside one interval, endpoints included.
Go through the list in order and mark only the numbers that are at least 10 and no more than 19.
The first value in that range is 12, and 9 is too small to count. Keep working down the list and tally the ones that qualify.
hintsEs: Una frecuencia es simplemente el conteo de cuántos valores caen dentro de un intervalo, incluyendo los extremos.
Recorre la lista en orden y marca solo los números que sean al menos 10 y no más de 19.
El primer valor en ese rango es 12, y el 9 es demasiado pequeño para contar. Sigue bajando por la lista y cuenta los que califican.
